properties.Session: EAPC Groups: Palliative Sedation. Evidence, guidelines, and controversies
properties.Chairs: Prof Lukas Radbruch, Prof Jeroen Hasselaar, Prof Sheila Payne, Dr Balazs Daniel Fulop

content:
Palliative sedation involves the intentional lowering of the level of consciousness in patients with life-limiting disease who are experiencing refractory suffering. There are many differences between European countries in its application and its use across palliative care practices. The session will start with explaining the main content of the updated framework on palliative sedation (published 2024), including some controversies. The session will continue with the main findings from a recent international multicenter study on palliative sedation (published 2024), showing a significant decrease of discomfort levels. The session will continue with experiences of relatives and healthcare professionals regarding palliative sedation (published 2025). Here, palliative sedation will be discussed as a complex intervention, with mixed experiences of relief and distress. Finally, the role of communication. Despite variations between settings, open dialogue with patients, families, and HCPs was considered valuable (publication 2025). The session will finish with space for discussion.
Attendees will learn which elements around palliative sedation reached expert consensus and which elements are still controversial in the debate surrounding palliative sedation, based on the updated framework for palliative sedation (published in 2024). In addition, highlights from European research will be shown regarding its medical aspects and the experiences of professionals and relatives. There will be space for a guided discussion.
Speakers:

1.	Prof Dr Lukas Radbruch, University of Bonn, Germany

2.	Prof Dr Jeroen Hasselaar, Radboudumc, the Netherlands 

3.	Prof Dr Sheila Payne, Lancaster University, England

4.	Dr Agnes Csikos, Pecs University, Hungary 

All speakers are members of the EAPC Task Force on Palliative Sedation.

properties.Session: TS: Integrating palliative care into respiratory care: Challenges, innovations, and European collaboration
properties.Chairs: Prof Philip Larkin, Dr Zuzana Křemenová

content:
Research into the management of symptoms and patient and family needs.

This themed session will feature three interconnected presentations.

Ágnes Csikós (University of Pécs) will discuss the challenges of integrating palliative care into respiratory care, including barriers at the patient, provider, and system levels, highlighting complexities such as unpredictable disease trajectories and the management of breathlessness.

Nancy Preston (Lancaster University) will present the ICLEAR intervention developed by Dr Paul Marsden at the Royal Preston Hospital in the UK, which helped integrate palliative care and improved communication between teams, reduced hospital admissions and enabled people to spend more time at home toward the end of life.

Luc Deliens (Vrije Universiteit Brussel) will introduce the EU PAL-COPD project, a large-scale, stepped-wedge RCT adapting and scaling the ICLEAR intervention across Europe. We will share preliminary findings from the first control wedge.

The session will conclude with a panel discussion inviting audience questions and reflections on the speakers’ experiences implementing ICLEAR in their respective countries.

Aims and learning objectives:

This session will highlight the importance of integrating palliative care into respiratory services for patients with advanced respiratory diseases. Participants will: Recognise the challenges and barriers to effective integration; Learn from the practical experiences of a UK study embedding palliative care within respiratory clinics; Gain insights into the EU PAL-COPD project, a European initiative focused on integrated palliative care in COPD. By the end of the session, attendees will be able to critically assess implementation strategies and explore ways to improve patient-centred care in respiratory services across diverse healthcare settings.

properties.Session: EAPC Groups: Strong Foundations, Shaky Grounds: LGBT+ Palliative Care in a Polarized World
properties.Chairs: Dr Katherine Bristowe, Mr Theodor Pilou Kruse, Dr Max Kleijberg

content:
This session focuses on the implementation of the EAPC’s LGBT+ palliative care guidelines across varying cultural and geopolitical contexts. Katherine Bristowe will outline current translation and adaptation efforts across Europe. Theodor Kruse will address the urgent and specific needs of trans communities under threat, highlighting the role of palliative care professionals in responding to crisis with advocacy and action. Max Kleijberg will ground the discussion in real-world examples from Sweden, exploring practical tools for healthcare teams to offer inclusive care. Together, these presentations offer insight into translating policy into practice, building intersectional care structures, and responding to an increasingly polarized world.

This session aims to explore how EAPC recommendations for LGBT+ inclusive palliative care are being translated into local contexts amid rising anti-LGBT+ sentiment. Participants will learn how to implement culturally sensitive and inclusive practices, especially for trans individuals facing systemic threats. The session also fosters critical reflection on the intersection of care, politics, and equity, offering practical tools and solidarity-driven frameworks for clinical, educational, and policy responses. 

Speakers:

Dr Katherine Bristowe – King’s College London, UK 
Theodor P. Kruse – Sygehus Lillebælt, Denmark 
Max Kleijberg – Mälardalen University / Karolinska Institutet, Sweden

All speakers are members of the EAPC Task Force on Palliative Care for LGBT+ People

TS: Emerging challenges in opioid prescribing for people with cancer
properties.Chairs: Prof Mette Asbjoern Neergaard, Prof Philip Larkin

content:
Research into Public Health in Palliative Care.The global cancer burden is growing, with projected 35.3 million new cases worldwide by 2050. Opioids remain the cornerstone of management for cancer-related symptoms, such as pain, dyspnea, and cough. As more people live with cancer, opioid use in this population warrants critical reexamination—particularly in the context of the ongoing opioid overdose epidemic. Yet access to these essential medications remains profoundly unequal: some high-income countries face a crisis of opioid overuse and associated harms, while most of the world’s population has little or no access to opioid analgesia.

This session will explore emerging issues in opioid prescribing for people with cancer, including stewardship strategies for those with comorbid opioid use disorder or elevated risk of overdose, and the global impact of diversion and restrictive regulation on access in low-, middle-, and high-income countries. Participants will be invited to discuss how to balance opioid safety with compassionate, equitable access worldwide.

Aims and learning objectives:
1. Describe the evolving role of opioids in cancer care amid the dual global crises of opioid excess in some settings and restricted access in others

2. Identify strategies for opioid stewardship in cancer care, including for those with opioid use disorder or elevated risk of opioid overdose

3. Describe the methods of opioid diversion, gaps in the opioid supply chain, and ways of addressing these gaps

4. Assess the impact of restrictive laws and regulations on opioid access for people with cancer in low-, middle-, and high-income countries
